items.title: Container port congestion smashes covid-era record
items.summary: Global container congestion has risen above the pandemic-era absolute peak, with Linerlytica estimating 4.3 million TEU waiting to berth. East Asia is driving much of the surge after tropical storms disrupted Chinese port operations, while Shanghai and Ningbo queues have reached unusually high levels.
items.logisticsImpact: Congestion removes effective vessel capacity even without fleet reductions, extending transit times, weakening schedule reliability and supporting higher freight and charter rates across global liner networks.

items.title: Fire Breaks Out On Saudi Oil Tanker Near Red Sea Port Of Yanbu After Houthi Attack
items.summary: A tanker west of Yanbu was struck by an unknown projectile and caught fire, according to UKMTO reporting cited by Marine Insight. Bahri confirmed its vessel Amzan was involved in an incident and said the crew was safe. Houthi claims about the weapon and attack remain independently unverified.
items.logisticsImpact: An attack near Yanbu raises security and insurance risk on a Red Sea route Saudi exporters can use to bypass Hormuz, potentially affecting tanker routing, premiums and energy-shipping capacity.

items.title: OFAC adds new Iran-related designations and expands sectoral sanctions actions
items.summary: OFAC added numerous Iran-related names to the SDN List and published new actions covering Iranian aviation, shipping, technology, gold and digital-asset sectors, alongside changes to Iran-related general licenses. The measures broaden the compliance perimeter for companies handling affected trade.
items.logisticsImpact: Forwarders, carriers, banks and cargo interests need refreshed sanctions screening across counterparties, vessels and transactions, with heightened exposure in shipping, aviation and Iran-linked payment chains.

items.title: Kremlin says it is acting to minimise impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russian grain exports
items.discovery: Global food and Black Sea logistics scan
items.summary: Russia said it is taking measures to reduce the effect of Ukrainian strikes on grain exports. Recent reciprocal attacks on Black Sea ports and vessels have shut grain terminals and forced delays or cancellations during peak export season, increasing uncertainty for major wheat-importing markets.
items.logisticsImpact: Black Sea disruption can tighten grain vessel availability, delay bulk loadings and push buyers toward more distant origins, increasing commodity prices, freight costs and voyage requirements.

items.title: Those behind hybrid attacks against Germany 'will pay,' Merz says, as officials find third drone at airport
items.summary: German investigators found another drone and suspected explosives linked to the earlier attempted attack around Leipzig/Halle Airport. The airport is a major cargo hub, hosts Antonov operations and previously diverted several cargo flights during the security incident. Attribution remains under investigation.
items.logisticsImpact: Persistent drone threats around a major European cargo hub can trigger diversions, security stoppages and additional screening, with knock-on effects for express networks, military logistics and time-critical freight.

items.title: Hormuz blockade causes project cargo build up
items.summary: Project-cargo carrier Chipolbrok says cargo for infrastructure and industrial projects is building up as restrictions around Hormuz disrupt normal shipment planning. The backlog highlights how geopolitical disruption is spilling beyond tanker and container trades into multipurpose and heavy-lift movements.
items.logisticsImpact: Project cargo has limited substitution options for vessel type, lifting capacity and port handling. Backlogs can therefore delay construction schedules, tie up specialized tonnage and raise charter and storage costs.

items.title: US calls transhipments a 'scam': Why do firms reroute goods, and how does Singapore manage this?
items.summary: U.S. scrutiny of alleged tariff-evasion transshipment is increasing attention on major hubs including Singapore. The Business Times reports U.S. authorities are using new analytical tools and already have authority to impose an additional 40% duty when goods are found to be transshipped to evade tariffs.
items.logisticsImpact: Importers and forwarders should expect greater origin verification, manifest scrutiny and supply-chain audits, especially where Chinese-origin inputs move through third countries before U.S. import.

items.title: Northern Star – Delos Wave 630N Shanghai Omission
items.summary: Maersk said Delos Wave 630N will omit Shanghai after adverse regional weather affected scheduling. Cargo planned for Shanghai discharge is being moved through alternative routings as the carrier tries to limit further delay to the service.
items.logisticsImpact: A Shanghai omission adds transshipment and connection risk for affected containers and is another operational signal of weather-driven schedule pressure feeding wider East Asian congestion.

items.title: U.S. removes Syria State Sponsor of Terrorism designation and updates sanctions relief
items.summary: The United States removed Syria's State Sponsor of Terrorism designation, removed HTS from the SDN List and updated related sanctions and export-control guidance. OFAC also revoked Syria General License 25 because the underlying designation changes made it unnecessary.
items.logisticsImpact: The changes can reopen compliant trade pathways, but shippers and brokers still need transaction-level screening because other sanctions, export controls and designated parties may continue to apply.

items.title: Impala opens $20m mineral logistics hub at Port of Arica
items.discovery: Latin America port and bulk logistics scan
items.summary: Impala Terminals opened a $20 million mineral handling and storage facility at Chile's Port of Arica, including an 11,100-square-metre warehouse, Rotainer containers and sealed truck transfers. The facility is intended to move Bolivian mineral storage away from the main port footprint.
items.logisticsImpact: Moving mineral storage outside the core terminal can free berth-side space, shorten handling cycles and expand Arica's capacity as a Pacific gateway for landlocked Bolivian trade.

items.title: Fewer than 20 ships transit key Strait of Hormuz over weekend, data shows
items.summary: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely reduced, with ship-tracking data showing only a small number of commodity-vessel transits over the weekend amid continuing regional conflict and restrictions.
items.logisticsImpact: Lower transit confidence can tighten tanker capacity, raise war-risk and insurance costs, complicate Gulf schedules and increase energy and freight costs well beyond the immediate route.

items.title: India's Iran exports set to fall further due to Dubai halt, U.S. sanctions
items.summary: Indian exporters are facing greater difficulty serving Iran as new sanctions and UAE restrictions interfere with payment and routing channels that have historically used Dubai.
items.logisticsImpact: Exporters may need alternative routes and payment structures while facing higher freight, insurance and compliance costs, particularly for food and pharmaceutical trade.

items.title: Looming U.S. sanctions on Iran put China oil buying in spotlight
items.summary: China's purchases of Iranian oil are under increasing scrutiny as additional sanctions threaten companies, financial channels and shipping networks connected to the trade.
items.logisticsImpact: Tighter enforcement can alter tanker routing, documentation, payment channels and origin declarations while increasing sanctions-screening requirements across energy supply chains.

items.title: The Hormuz crude volume debate masks the real shortage of refined fuels
items.summary: Reduced flows of refined products into Asia are emerging as a major consequence of the Gulf disruption, with diesel, jet fuel and gasoline availability under pressure even where crude supply appears less constrained.
items.logisticsImpact: Higher refined-fuel costs can feed directly into aviation, trucking, vessel bunkers and industrial distribution, making the disruption relevant across transport modes rather than only tanker shipping.

items.title: Mark Carney sensibly avoids stepping in fertilizer
items.summary: Escalating U.S.-Canada tariff measures are increasing pressure on automotive, steel and other cross-border supply chains as Canada looks for ways to reduce its dependence on the U.S. market.
items.logisticsImpact: Tariffs can shift sourcing, landed costs, origin planning and truck or rail volumes across the border while encouraging longer-term diversification of North American supply chains.
